name: Burkina Faso
notShared: Own model, own engine, own reference code.
criteria: easy to remember and easy to get (first)
compound is the unit, gate is the entrance
official addresses first: use the commune's door addresses where they exist; postcode as pointer; parcels as cross-references

existing.verdict: coarse official postal codes (commune / urban zone level), not door-level

postcode.structure: d1 region, d1-2 province, d3-4 quartier/commune/agency, d5 type (0 commune or quartier, 1-8 agency)
postcode.matchToCommunes: model/units/communes.csv (294 exact, 55 spelling to verify, 1 manual, Komsilga none)

existing.streetAddressing: Ouagadougou/Bobo street codes 'Rue <secteur>.<order>' + metric door numbers; AMB/EU/PASIU renewal since 2021
existing.parcels: Décret 2012-1006 section/îlot/parcelle, digits only; DGI eCadastre / SyC@D (sif.bf)

remembered.contains: place words people already use + 3-5 digits; no letters to learn; unique in the whole country on its own (no position, no town after a comma)
remembered.spokenFr: pairs from the left as phone numbers: 41 17 'quarante-et-un dix-sept'; town form 'secteur quinze, Ouaga, quarante-huit deux cent dix-sept'

machine.checkInput: village: nameId (5 digits, frozen national id of the normalised name) + postcode + kindDigit(2) + index + number; secteur: postcode + kindDigit(1) + secteur + number (the postcode is the town word)
machine.note: secteur numbers in examples are illustrative until secteur maps are obtained
machine.validity: a village code is valid only if its number lies in one of that village's blocks of its name's range

plate.where: only where no official address exists

spot.digits: 4 per axis; 5 on an axis wider than 99.99 km (Matiakoali, Tin-Akoff, Ouo, Pama)
spot.frame: per commune: origin = SW box corner floored to 0.01 deg; reference latitude = box centre rounded to 0.01 deg; local equirectangular metres (110574 m/deg lat, 111320 cos(latc) m/deg lon); frozen in model/units/frames.json
spot.why: Burkina spans UTM 30 and 31; a commune-local metric grid reference is readable on paper maps

villages.rule: all villages/hamlets whose PLATE name has the same normalised key draw from ONE national range for that name, one frozen block per village
villages.normalisation: NFKD accents and case folded; leading Q/Quartier/Hameau/Village de and articles le/la/les/l' dropped; spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, dots dropped; tch=c, dj=j, gh=g, ph=f, ou=w=u, gu before i/e=g; doubled letters single; official qualifiers kept (Bissiga-Peulh != Bissiga); engine: bf_engine.name_key
villages.block: compounds x 2 rounded up to a multiple of 10, minimum 20; laid in register order (postcode, index) at first issue
villages.digits: per name: smallest of 3,4,5 whose range holds all blocks with the top tenth spare
villages.generic: labels that are not names (village, Campement d'éleveurs, Site de recasement...) are renamed with the commune before issue; no block
villages.tooLargeAlone: a village whose block exceeds a 5-digit range is split by named quartiers/secteurs before issue
villages.qualifier: if a name's blocks together exceed 5 digits: bare name for the blocks that fit in register order, commune as qualifier for the others ('Yargo-Kaya'), decided once and listed in model/areas/name-ranges.json; split quartier areas named by a common quarter word (Natenga, Nayiri, Tanghin, Zongo) take the village as qualifier ('Boassa-Zongo')
villages.data: model/areas/name-ranges.json (built by tools/name-ranges.py from model/stats/area-compounds.csv); aliasKeys map official names to plate names

secteurs.rule: the town word is part of the code by rule: 'Secteur 15 Ouaga · 48 217' != 'Secteur 15 Bobo · 48 217'
secteurs.why: every urban commune numbers secteurs from 1; a shared 'Secteur 1' range would hold one block per town (an average Ouagadougou secteur alone needs 22,420 numbers; 183 other communes hold ~1.25 M compounds around town nodes): over 5 digits
secteurs.townWord: commune name under the plate rule; documented short forms Ouaga (10000, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ouagadougou), Bobo (90000, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobo_people), Fada (75000, fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fada_N'Gourma); full names are aliases; 18 town words over the limit or ambiguous are flagged needsCouncilChoice

nationalNames.check: Damm over nameId + postcode + kind + index + number (village), postcode + kind + secteur + number (secteur); out-of-block numbers invalid; optional check on the remembered form
nationalNames.stability: blocks frozen at issue, never renumbered; new same-named village = new block from the name's spare; full block = extension block from the spare; spare used up = commune qualifier; renamed village keeps its block, new name is an alias

counts.source: model/stats/area-compounds.csv (design register villages + OSM town nodes; 10% national footprint sample x 10 x 0.546)

nationalNames.rule: the remembered code must be unique nationally on its own: village names repeat across the country, and context (position, town after a comma) is rejected because a code must work when said aloud to someone elsewhere

plateNames.limit: plate name at most 12 characters (NFC; letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes count one) and at most 2 words (linking words de/du/des/la/le/l'/et/sur/en/au/aux/à and Tamasheq n not counted; a hyphen separates words); no digit
plateNames.names: officialName (small print, never required) + plateName (in the code); typing the official name decodes when it maps to one plate name (alias); an alias claimed by two plate names or equal to another plate name is dropped and listed
plateNames.derivation: documented short form with source; else clean (brackets, after slash, generic words Q/Quartier/Lieu-dit/Village de/Cité/Lotissement/Zone/Secteur/Hameau/Campement); else St/Ste abbreviation; else most distinctive run of whole words; never a word cut
burkinaRules: ethnic/status qualifiers (Peulh, Foulbé, Mossi, Silmi, Rimaïbé, Yarcé, Gourmantché, Bella, Traditionnel, Nouveau), Mooré Yiri/Tenga/Naba, Fulfuldé Ouro/Wouro are weak: never a plate alone; a short form dropping one goes to the commune
a short form dropping a number goes to the commune
a hyphenated name too long goes to the commune with its parts as candidates
no short form equal to a commune, province, region or big city of the region; nor the area's own commune or another place of the same commune
plateNames.council: needsCouncilChoice + plateCandidates (<= 3) + plateReason; first candidate provisional; the commune confirms before first issue; names with no fitting candidate cannot be issued (engine refuses)

examples.Debere Boulga: Boulga (shares the Boulga range with Boulga, Pensa; decodes apart by block)
examples.Gambo (moulin): Gambo (flagged: another Gambo in the commune)

plateNames.data: model/areas/register.json (plate fields per village), model/areas/town-words.json, model/stats/name-stats.json
plateNames.rule: the name in the code is short (at most 12 characters, 2 words) so that it can be said, written and painted on a gate

check.detects: every single-digit error, every adjacent transposition

optionsEvaluated.verdict: rejected: 7 digits in Ouagadougou (616,565 compounds x2)
rejected: 6 digits, zone codes not known by heart
cross-reference only: lotissement plots only, ~434k of ~1.26M digitised
used as the address where it exists, shown first; the N-Ways code sits beside it

urban.source: commune secteur maps (2009) or PASIU database — not yet obtained
urban.digits: 5 in Ouagadougou (616,565 compounds / 55 secteurs = 11,210; x2 = 22,420 <= 90,000); 4 or 5 in Bobo-Dioulasso (176,300 / 33 = 5,343)

rural.index: V001-V999 per commune (machine form only); numbers come from the village's block in its name's national range
rural.source: OpenStreetMap and GeoNames named places (model/areas/register.json); the INSD village list will add official names as aliases

codeAreas.split: an area with compounds x 2 > its range is split by named quartiers before issue; longer number only if no names
codeAreas.frozen: area polygons, indices and name blocks frozen at first issue; renames and renumbering update aliases only
codeAreas.capacityRule: secteur: compounds x 2 <= 9 x 10^(digits-1); village: compounds x 2 <= block, name blocks <= 0.9 x 9 x 10^(digits-1)

numbering.order: Hilbert curve, order 16, over the code area's box, on compound centroids (area-weighted)
numbering.range: secteur: 10^(d-1) .. 10^d - 1; village: its frozen block [lo, hi] in its name's national range
numbering.tailReserve: top third of the range or block
numbering.newCompound: free number between Hilbert neighbours closest to the midpoint, else lowest free tail number; full village block -> extension block from the name's spare
numbering.never: reused; demolished = retired; split = larger part keeps; merge = oldest survives, other becomes alias

compound.unit: concession / cour / plot (walled or not), one primary gate

grouping.test: centroid inside closed OSM barrier=wall|fence|hedge <= 6000 m2
structure < 25 m2 joins nearest >= 25 m2 within 8 m gap
structures < 40 m2 within 3 m chain, max 25
'these buildings are one home', 'this is the gate' by residents, confirmed by arrivals

compound.estates: walled areas > 6000 m2 with many compounds = estate/cité/camp: estate gate -> compound gate
reverseCases: cour commune / célibatorium: one compound, multi-household
immeuble: one compound, flats not coded
front-wall boutiques: extra entrances or own compound
cité behind one gate: estate level

inference.bonus: +0.05 per agreeing source; residential + commercial -> mixed 0.6

steps: stand at gate: GPS averaged a few seconds + one gate photo

outline: tap corners on imagery | AR walk inside the wall (ARKit/ARCore, anchored by averaged GPS, checked vs imagery/footprints) | import survey plan or lotissement parcel (beacons typed or photographed)
provisional code = next reserved number in the area
confirmed by arrivals/deliveries, no dispute, or new imagery
safeguards: an address is not a land title
gate on outline, plausible size, closed loop, GPS vs AR agreement
offline: spot code at once; compound code at next connection

legal.surveyors: cadastre or géomètre-expert (Ordre des Géomètres-Experts du Burkina)
legal.norms: Décret 2012-444: markers <= 7 cm; sketches in non-developed zones <= 3 m
legal.datum: référentiel national (not named in text; to confirm with IGB; IGB GNSS-CORS 13 stations)

public: every compound code with its entrance, spot code and building profile
private: Add-my-home photos (gate photo shown only to people navigating there, never published in open data)
privacy.travelAdvisory: the area table marks communes under the UK FCDO's advice against all travel (alert_zone) as context; every code is published; displaced-people sites are never published

distribution: N-Ways app: 'Mon adresse', one-tap share (WhatsApp/SMS link)
notOffered: SMS lookup service (possible later option only)

coverage.area: Readdressed arrondissements of Ouagadougou (1, 2, 5, 12; 2023 pilot arrondissements)
coverage.official: commune street code 'Rue <secteur>.<order>' + door number (AMB/EU, PASIU)
coverage.data: PASIU platforms 'Easy Geo', 'Webmapping grand Ouaga data'; not open; request from Commune de Ouagadougou + AMB under a data-sharing agreement
coverage.nways: import, show exactly as written, keep in sync; add gate, building profile, spot code; no N-Ways number or plate

coverage.data: Commune de Bobo-Dioulasso / PASIU; not open

coverage.area: Non-loti zones, secteurs not readdressed, other towns, villages

coverage.official: La Poste postcode (commune/zone; not an address)
coverage.nways: pointer: machine prefix; attribute of official addresses

officialImport.display: exactly as officially written, e.g. 'Rue 15.123, porte 45, Ouagadougou'
officialImport.sync: re-import on each communal release (or monthly feed); diff; official changes win; N-Ways never edits official records, only reports suspected errors to the commune
officialImport.whenReaddressedLater: N-Ways code issued before becomes an alias of the official address; plates replaced by the commune's

officialFirst.applies: wherever a commune has given an address, that official address is shown first, exactly as written; the compound keeps its N-Ways code beside it, with the gate position, building profile and spot code. Postcodes and P.O. boxes are not addresses but stay as pointers.
officialFirst.rule: where the State has given an address, it is used as written and shown first; nothing competes with it
